close_reason: Decision record landed at parse::resolve_args doc — explicit cross-reference to resolve_args_atomic_on_partial_failure test, plus rationale defending two-phase shape against future 'simplification' suggestions.
description:
crate-jmap-server/src/parse.rs:131-195 — resolve_args is implemented as two phases:

  Phase 1: Walk every #-prefixed key, resolve each ResultReference WITHOUT mutating args. Collect (ref_key, plain_key, resolved_value) into a Vec.
  Phase 2: If and only if all resolutions succeeded, apply the mutations atomically (remove #key, insert plain_key).

A future contributor will reasonably suggest "this is one extra pass over the keys — just resolve-and-mutate inline, that's simpler". That suggestion is WRONG and the current shape should be defended.

Why two-phase is correct:
  - RFC 8620 §3.7 semantics are atomic: if ANY ResultReference fails to resolve, the entire method call gets invalidResultReference. A partial-mutation would leave a malformed args object that handlers could observe.
  - Even though resolve_args returns an Err and the dispatcher converts that to error_invocation, the caller's `args` Value is still observable by reference (the function takes &mut Value). A test that checks args contents on error path would see a partial state under inline-mutation.
  - Test resolve_args_atomic_on_partial_failure (parse.rs:406) directly encodes this contract: "args must be completely unchanged on error".

A future reviewer asking "why the extra Vec allocation" should be pointed at the atomicity test as the rationale. Without two-phase, that test would fail. Document with a brief comment block linking the two-phase structure to the atomicity contract.
title: Two-phase atomic resolve_args is the right shape
